description: Hi! I'm participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge. I create a fun, educational experience for kids. Let's combine our skills, learn something new, and have a great hackathon weekend!
summary: AstroNovas Kids is our idea for a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer, a game made for kids. In the game, a child becomes a young astronaut running a small outpost on the Moon or Mars. They have to keep oxygen, food, power and radiation protection in balance, and every choice has a result. The game has a low-gravity jumping mini game that shows how gravity works, and short story missions, like a sudden dust storm on Mars, where the player decides what to do next. This submission presents the concept, the game design and a slide demo. Our goal is to make space learning fun and easy for children.
details:
AstroNovas Kids is our concept for a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer, a game where kids learn to run an outpost on the Moon or Mars. It has three parts. In the Anti-Gravity Training mini game, the player controls an astronaut in low gravity and tries to land at the right spot. In the resource management part, the player keeps oxygen, food, solar power and the radiation shield in balance. For example, watering the plants gives oxygen, but it also needs power, so the player has to choose carefully. In Story Mode, each level begins with a short story, like a dust storm on Mars, and the player decides what to do next.

Kids can learn basic physics, problem solving and decision making by playing instead of just reading. The game also shows them that in space, every resource is connected to the others.

We want children to feel excited about space and to understand that real missions need careful planning and teamwork. We hope it makes space learning feel fun and easy for young learners.

At this stage we worked on the idea and the game design, and we made a slide presentation to explain it. We have not built the game yet. For building it in the future, we are thinking of beginner-friendly tools like Scratch or MIT App Inventor.

The idea comes from kids, for kids. Instead of only learning facts, the child becomes the astronaut and sees the result of every choice they make.

While planning, we thought about simple controls, friendly and colorful pictures, short levels, and stories that suit young children.
